claim: Long-term memory (LTM) is believed to be stored in the brain as changes in synaptic connections.
source: Long-term memory (LTM) is believed to be stored in the brain as changes in synaptic connections.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific belief presented in the abstract.

claim: Cocultures of Aplysia sensory and motor neurons were trained with spaced pulses of serotonin, which induces long-term facilitation.
source: Cocultures of Aplysia sensory and motor neurons were trained with spaced pulses of serotonin, which induces long-term facilitation.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used in the study.

claim: Serotonin (5HT) triggered growth of new presynaptic varicosities, a synaptic mechanism of long-term sensitization.
source: Serotonin (5HT) triggered growth of new presynaptic varicosities, a synaptic mechanism of long-term sensitization.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claim: Following 5HT training, two antimnemonic treatments—reconsolidation blockade and inhibition of PKM—caused the number of presynaptic varicosities to revert to the original, pretraining value.
source: Following 5HT training, two antimnemonic treatments—reconsolidation blockade and inhibition of PKM—caused the number of presynaptic varicosities to revert to the original, pretraining value.
evidence: This is a key finding from the experimental data.

claim: The final synaptic structure was not achieved by targeted retraction of the 5HT-induced varicosities but, rather, by an apparently arbitrary retraction of both 5HT-induced and original synapses.
source: Surprisingly, the final synaptic structure was not achieved by targeted retraction of the 5HT-induced varicosities but, rather, by an apparently arbitrary retraction of both 5HT-induced and original synapses.
evidence: This is a surprising finding from tracking individual varicosities over time.

claim: The LTM for sensitization persists covertly after its apparent elimination by the same antimnemonic treatments that erase learning-related synaptic growth.
source: In addition, we find evidence that the LTM for sensitization persists covertly after its apparent elimination by the same antimnemonic treatments that erase learning-related synaptic growth.
evidence: This is a key conclusion from the behavioral reinstatement experiments.

claim: These results challenge the idea that stable synapses store long-term memories.
source: These results challenge the idea that stable synapses store long-term memories.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Ramón Y Cajal proposed more than a century ago that long-term memories are expressed in the brain, in part, by changes in synaptic connectivity.
source: There is significant empirical support for the idea, proposed by Ramón Y Cajal more than a century ago (Cajal, 1894), that long-term memories are expressed in the brain, in part, by changes in synaptic connectivity.
evidence: This is a historical citation to Cajal's work.

claim: Memories are maintained by persistent molecular and cellular alterations in synaptic structures themselves.
source: A corollary of this idea, accepted by many, if not most, modern neuroscientists, is that memories are maintained by persistent molecular and cellular alterations in synaptic structures themselves (Bailey and Kandel, 2008; Kandel et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement of current scientific consensus supported by citations.

claim: Sensitization of the gill- and siphon-withdrawal reflex in Aplysia exhibits a long-term (≥24 hr) form.
source: Sensitization of the withdrawal reflex exhibits a long-term (≥24 hr) form (Pinsker et al., 1973) due, in part, to long-term facilitation (LTF) of the monosynaptic connection between the sensory and motor neurons that mediate the reflex (Frost et al., 1985).
evidence: This is a well-established finding in the Aplysia literature, supported by citations.

claim: Long-term sensitization is due, in part, to long-term facilitation (LTF) of the monosynaptic connection between the sensory and motor neurons that mediate the reflex.
source: Sensitization of the withdrawal reflex exhibits a long-term (≥24 hr) form (Pinsker et al., 1973) due, in part, to long-term facilitation (LTF) of the monosynaptic connection between the sensory and motor neurons that mediate the reflex (Frost et al., 1985).
evidence: This is a well-established finding supported by citation.

claim: The monosynaptic sensorimotor connection can be reconstituted in dissociated cell culture.
source: Importantly, the monosynaptic sensorimotor connection can be reconstituted in dissociated cell culture, and LTF of the in vitro synapse can be induced by training with pulses of serotonin (5HT), the monoaminergic neurotransmitter that mediates sensitization in Aplysia (Brunelli et al., 1976; Glanzman et al., 1989; Marinesco and Carew, 2002).
evidence: This is a well-established methodological approach supported by citations.

claim: LTF of the in vitro synapse can be induced by training with pulses of serotonin (5HT), the monoaminergic neurotransmitter that mediates sensitization in Aplysia.
source: Importantly, the monosynaptic sensorimotor connection can be reconstituted in dissociated cell culture, and LTF of the in vitro synapse can be induced by training with pulses of serotonin (5HT), the monoaminergic neurotransmitter that mediates sensitization in Aplysia (Brunelli et al., 1976; Glanzman et al., 1989; Marinesco and Carew, 2002).
evidence: This is a well-established finding supported by citations.

claim: A reminder stimulus delivered to an animal that serves to reactivate the LTM for a previous learning experience, followed by treatment with an inhibitor of protein synthesis, will apparently eliminate the LTM.
source: Here, a stimulus is delivered to an animal that serves to reactivate the LTM for a previous learning experience. If, immediately after delivery of this reminder, the animal is treated with an inhibitor of protein synthesis (Nader et al., 2000), or subjected to electroconvulsive shock (Misanin et al., 1968), the LTM will be apparently eliminated.
evidence: This describes the reconsolidation blockade phenomenon, supported by citations.

claim: Inhibition of the constitutively active catalytic fragment of the atypical protein kinase Cζ (PKMζ) can apparently erase LTM permanently.
source: Another manipulation that can apparently erase LTM permanently is inhibition of the constitutively active catalytic fragment of the atypical protein kinase Cζ; the ongoing activity of this catalytic fragment, named PKMζ, appears to be required for the maintenance of several forms of LTM in mammals (Sacktor, 2011); inhibition of PKMζ, in the absence of a reminder, has been reported to abolish consolidated memory (but see Lee et al., 2013; Volk et al., 2013).
evidence: This describes another antimnemonic manipulation, supported by citations.

claim: The synaptic memory for LTF of in vitro sensorimotor connections can be apparently eliminated when sensorimotor cocultures are treated with a protein synthesis inhibitor following reminder training.
source: We, and others, have shown that the synaptic memory for LTF of in vitro sensorimotor connections can be apparently eliminated when sensorimotor cocultures are treated with a protein synthesis inhibitor following reminder training (Cai et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2012; Hu and Schacher, 2014).
evidence: This is a finding from previous work by the authors and others, supported by citations.

claim: Inhibiting the activity of PKM Apl III, the constitutively active fragment of the Aplysia atypical protein kinase C (PKC Apl III), erases consolidated LTF.
source: In addition, inhibiting the activity of PKM Apl III, the constitutively active fragment of the Aplysia atypical protein kinase C (PKC Apl III) (Villareal et al., 2009; Cai et al., 2011; Bougie et al., 2012), also erases consolidated LTF (Cai et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a finding from previous work by the authors, supported by citations.

claim: LTF is mediated partly by the growth of new sensory neuron varicosities.
source: LTF is mediated partly by the growth of new sensory neuron varicosities (Glanzman et al., 1990; Bailey and Kandel, 2008).
evidence: This is a well-established finding supported by citations.

claim: The 5X5HT training produced a significant increase in the number of presynaptic varicosities contacting the MN.
source: As previously reported (Glanzman et al., 1990), the 5X5HT training produced a significant increase in the number of presynaptic varicosities contacting the MN (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The reminder pulse of 5HT coupled with inhibition of protein synthesis caused the number of varicosities to revert to the pretraining (0 hr) value in the 5X5HT-1X5HT-Aniso group.
source: The reminder pulse of 5HT coupled with inhibition of protein synthesis caused the number of varicosities to revert to the pretraining (0 hr) value in the 5X5HT-1X5HT-Aniso group.
evidence: This is a key finding from the experimental data.

claim: This structural result parallels the electrophysiological results previously reported for Aplysia sensorimotor cocultures.
source: This structural result parallels the electrophysiological results previously reported for Aplysia sensorimotor cocultures (Cai et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2012; Hu and Schacher, 2014), and provides additional support for the notion that 1X5HT reactivated the synaptic memory induced by the 5X5HT training.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the current structural findings to previous electrophysiological findings.

claim: Many of the 5HT-induced SN varicosities in the 5HT-No reconsolidation/No blockade group did not persist until the final imaging session.
source: First, many of the 5HT-induced SN varicosities in the 5HT-No reconsolidation/No blockade group did not persist until the final imaging session (Figures 2A and 3A); instead, there was significant retraction of the 5HT-induced varicosities between 24 and 48 hr in this group.
evidence: This is a direct observation from tracking individual varicosities, shown in Figures 2A and 3A.

claim: There was significant retraction of the 5HT-induced varicosities between 24 and 48 hr in the 5HT-No reconsolidation/No blockade group.
source: First, many of the 5HT-induced SN varicosities in the 5HT-No reconsolidation/No blockade group did not persist until the final imaging session (Figures 2A and 3A); instead, there was significant retraction of the 5HT-induced varicosities between 24 and 48 hr in this group.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claim: There was also retraction of the original varicosities during the 24-48 hr period in the 5HT-No reconsolidation/No blockade group.
source: Second, there was also retraction of the original varicosities during this period (Figures 2B and 3A).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, shown in Figures 2B and 3A.

claim: There was substantial growth of new varicosities in all trained groups between 24 and 48 hr.
source: A third unexpected finding was the substantial growth of new varicosities in all trained groups between 24 and 48 hr; the amount of the growth was significantly greater, however, in the 5-HT-No reconsolidation/No blockade cocultures than in the 5X5HT-1X5HT-Aniso group (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The 5X5HT trained cocultures subjected to reconsolidation blockade exhibited significantly more retraction and significantly less growth of varicosities during the 24–48 hr period than did the other trained cocultures.
source: Thus, the 5X5HT trained cocultures subjected to reconsolidation blockade exhibited significantly more retraction and significantly less growth of varicosities during the 24–48 hr period than did the other trained cocultures.
evidence: This is a summary of the comparative findings from the experimental data.

claim: There was greater retraction of 5HT-induced varicosities than of original varicosities between 24–48 hr in the 5HT-No reconsolidation/No blockade group.
source: Interestingly, whereas there was greater retraction of 5HT-induced varicosities than of original varicosities between 24–48 hr in the 5HT-No reconsolidation/No blockade group, the retraction of 5HT-induced varicosities and original varicosities did not differ in the 5X5HT-1X5HT-Aniso group (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The retraction of 5HT-induced varicosities and original varicosities did not differ in the 5X5HT-1X5HT-Aniso group.
source: Interestingly, whereas there was greater retraction of 5HT-induced varicosities than of original varicosities between 24–48 hr in the 5HT-No reconsolidation/No blockade group, the retraction of 5HT-induced varicosities and original varicosities did not differ in the 5X5HT-1X5HT-Aniso group (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: PKM Apl III is a homolog of mammalian PKMζ.
source: PKM Apl III, a homolog of mammalian PKMζ (Sacktor, 2011), is formed from the atypical Aplysia protein kinase C (PKC Apl III) (Bougie et al., 2009) by calpain-dependent cleavage; furthermore, this cleavage is induced by prolonged treatment with 5HT (Bougie et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about the molecular identity of PKM Apl III, supported by citations.

claim: PKM Apl III is formed from the atypical Aplysia protein kinase C (PKC Apl III) by calpain-dependent cleavage.
source: PKM Apl III, a homolog of mammalian PKMζ (Sacktor, 2011), is formed from the atypical Aplysia protein kinase C (PKC Apl III) (Bougie et al., 2009) by calpain-dependent cleavage; furthermore, this cleavage is induced by prolonged treatment with 5HT (Bougie et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about the formation of PKM Apl III, supported by citations.

claim: The cleavage of PKC Apl III to form PKM Apl III is induced by prolonged treatment with 5HT.
source: PKM Apl III, a homolog of mammalian PKMζ (Sacktor, 2011), is formed from the atypical Aplysia protein kinase C (PKC Apl III) (Bougie et al., 2009) by calpain-dependent cleavage; furthermore, this cleavage is induced by prolonged treatment with 5HT (Bougie et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about the induction of PKM Apl III formation, supported by citation.

claim: Inhibition of PKM Apl III abolished both consolidated long-term sensitization and LTF.
source: In previous behavioral and electrophysiological investigations we found that inhibition of PKM Apl III, either with the pseudosubstrate sequence of the regulatory domain of atypical PKC (ZIP) or with chelerythrine, a PKC inhibitor selective for PKM at low concentrations (Ling et al., 2002; Villareal et al., 2009), abolished both consolidated long-term sensitization and LTF (Cai et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a finding from previous work by the authors, supported by citations.

claim: The 5X5HT training produced a significant net increase in the number of presynaptic varicosities in the two trained groups at 24 hr.
source: As before, the 5X5HT training produced a significant net increase in the number of presynaptic varicosities in the two trained groups at 24 hr (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The net increase in varicosity number persisted in the 5X5HT group, but was reversed in 5X5HT-Chel group at 48 hr.
source: This net increase persisted in the 5X5HT group, but was reversed in 5X5HT-Chel group at 48 hr.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claim: The varicosities in the 5X5HT-Chel group exhibited significantly greater retraction and significantly less growth between 24 and 48 hr than those in the 5X5HT group.
source: The varicosities in the 5X5HT-Chel group exhibited significantly greater retraction and significantly less growth between 24 and 48 hr than those in the 5X5HT group, resulting in an overall loss of varicosities.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claim: The number of varicosities in the 5X5HT-Chel group at 48 hr was returned to the value at 0 hr.
source: Thus, the number of varicosities in the 5X5HT-Chel group at 48 hr was returned to the value at 0 hr.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claim: Inhibiting PKM Apl III, like reconsolidation blockade, engages a homeostatic mechanism that resets the presynaptic varicosities in sensorimotor cocultures to the number present prior to training.
source: This result indicates that inhibiting PKM Apl III, like reconsolidation blockade (Figure 1C), engages a homeostatic mechanism that resets the presynaptic varicosities in sensorimotor cocultures to the number present prior to training.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data.

claim: There was equal retraction of 5HT-induced and original varicosities in the 5X5HT-Chel cocultures during 24–48 hr.
source: Another similarity between the morphological effects of reconsolidation blockade and inhibition of PKM was that there was equal retraction of 5HT-induced and original varicosities in the 5X5HT-Chel cocultures during 24–48 hr, whereas, as before, the retraction of 5HT-induced varicosities was greater in the 5X5HT cocultures during this period (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was significant growth and retraction of SN varicosities, both original and new, over the 48 hr of the experiments in Control cocultures.
source: Inspection of the synaptic structure of the Control cocultures revealed a complex underlying pattern of structural change similar to that observed in the reconsolidation experiment. There was significant growth and retraction of SN varicosities, both original and new, over the 48 hr of the experiments (Figures 6 and 1B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data, shown in Figures 6 and 1B.

claim: The structural dynamism in Control cocultures contrasted with the constancy of overall varicosity number in these cocultures.
source: This structural dynamism contrasted with the constancy of overall varicosity number in these cocultures (Figures 1C and 4B), as well as with the stability of the sensorimotor EPSP amplitude observed in Control cocultures over similar time periods in our earlier studies (Cai et al., 2011, 2012).
evidence: This is an observation comparing the dynamic changes in individual varicosities with the stable overall number.

claim: Three additional bouts of tail shocks did not induce LTM in naïve animals.
source: Importantly, the three additional bouts of sensitization training did not induce LTM in naïve animals (Control-Veh-3XTrained; Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the behavioral experiments, shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Three bouts of training completely restored LTM following its disruption by reconsolidation blockade.
source: However, the three bouts of training completely restored LTM following its disruption by reconsolidation blockade (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is a key finding from the behavioral experiments, shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Animals treated with chelerythrine exhibited no LTS at 48 hr.
source: 24 hr after the original sensitization training the animals received an intrahemocoel injection of chelerythrine (Figure 8A). Animals treated with chelerythrine exhibited no LTS at 48 hr (Figure 8B), confirming our previous finding (Cai et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the behavioral experiments, shown in Figure 8B.

claim: The modest additional training reinstated LTS following its apparent erasure by chelerythrine, but did not produce LTS in the control animals.
source: The modest additional training reinstated LTS following its apparent erasure by chelerythrine, but did not produce LTS in the control animals (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is a key finding from the behavioral experiments, shown in Figure 8B.

claim: TSA treatment blocked the disruption of LTS by chelerythrine.
source: TSA treatment blocked the disruption of LTS by chelerythrine (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the behavioral experiments, shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The injection of TSA 24 hr after training by itself did not alter LTS.
source: The injection of TSA 24 hr after training by itself did not alter LTS (5XTrained-TSA group).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the behavioral experiments.

claim: One of chelerythrine's antimnemonic actions is to reverse histone acetylation induced by LTS training.
source: These results indicate that one of chelerythrine's antimnemonic actions is to reverse histone acetylation induced by LTS training.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the TSA blocking experiment.

claim: Animals that received three bouts of shocks after an injection of TSA exhibited LTS at 24 hr, whereas animals that received the shocks after an injection of vehicle did not.
source: 24 hr later the animals that received three bouts of shocks after an injection of TSA exhibited LTS, whereas animals that received the shocks after an injection of vehicle did not (Figure 9D).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the behavioral experiments, shown in Figure 9D.

claim: HDAC inhibition facilitates the induction of LTM in Aplysia.
source: Thus, HDAC inhibition facilitates the induction of LTM in Aplysia.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TSA facilitation experiment.

claim: The persistence of sensitization-related LTM in Aplysia does not require the persistence of the synaptic connections generated during learning.
source: The present morphological results, together with those of our previous behavioral and electrophysiological investigations (Cai et al., 2011, 2012), suggest that the persistence of sensitization-related LTM in Aplysia does not require the persistence of the synaptic connections generated during learning.
evidence: This is a key conclusion drawn from the combined morphological and behavioral findings.

claim: LTM appears to be regulated by a homeostatic mechanism that specifies the net synaptic strength according to experience.
source: Rather, LTM appears to be regulated by a homeostatic mechanism that specifies the net synaptic strength according to experience.
evidence: This is a key conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Following 5X5HT stimulation, the number of presynaptic varicosities in the sensorimotor cocultures increased to a new overall value, and that this value was maintained despite the appearance and disappearance of individual varicosities.
source: Following 5X5HT stimulation, we observed that the number of presynaptic varicosities in the sensorimotor cocultures increased to a new overall value, and that this value was maintained despite the appearance and disappearance of individual varicosities.
evidence: This is a summary of the key morphological findings.

claim: Blockade of memory reconsolidation, or inhibition of PKM, reset the number of varicosities to the original, non-facilitated value.
source: Furthermore, blockade of memory reconsolidation, or inhibition of PKM, reset the number of varicosities to the original, non-facilitated value.
evidence: This is a summary of the key morphological findings.

claim: The resetting of varicosity number was produced by a complex reorganization that involved retraction of both 5HT-induced and original varicosities, as well as growth of new, additional varicosities.
source: Remarkably, this resetting did not result from the straightforward retraction of the varicosities that appeared by 24 hr after 5X5HT stimulation, varicosities whose growth coincides with LTF (Glanzman et al., 1990); rather, the resetting was produced by a complex reorganization that involved retraction of both 5HT-induced and original varicosities, as well as growth of new, additional varicosities.
evidence: This is a summary of the key morphological findings.

claim: For any given sensorimotor connection, the homeostatic regulatory mechanism appeared indifferent to the identities of the particular presynaptic varicosities and, presumably, active zones that mediated baseline synaptic transmission and synaptic facilitation.
source: Thus, for any given sensorimotor connection, the homeostatic regulatory mechanism appeared indifferent to the identities of the particular presynaptic varicosities and, presumably, active zones (Schacher et al., 1990), that mediated baseline synaptic transmission and synaptic facilitation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the morphological findings.

claim: Synapses are not 'tagged' with respect to memory storage, at least for a connection involving a single SN and a single MN.
source: Our data argue that synapses are not 'tagged' with respect to memory storage, at least for a connection involving a single SN and a single MN; the data may therefore reflect a fundamental distinction between the cellular and molecular processes of LTM storage and those of LTM induction in Aplysia, in which synaptic tagging plays a critical role (Martin et al., 1997).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the morphological findings.

claim: Synaptic change is an expression mechanism, rather than a storage mechanism, for LTM in Aplysia.
source: The data also suggest that synaptic change is an expression mechanism, rather than a storage mechanism, for LTM in Aplysia (although see below).
evidence: This is a key conclusion drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: Neither reconsolidation blockade nor inhibition of PKM caused the varicosity number to drop below the starting value.
source: Importantly, neither reconsolidation blockade nor inhibition of PKM caused the varicosity number to drop below the starting value.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claim: The homeostatic mechanism toggles between two all-or-none states, a facilitated, sensitization-related state and a nonfacilitated one.
source: This result provides additional evidence for the operation of a homeostatic regulatory mechanism, and suggests that the homeostatic mechanism toggles between two all-or-none states, a facilitated, sensitization-related state and a nonfacilitated one.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental findings.

claim: There must also be a third state, synaptic depression, in which the strength of the sensorimotor connection is reduced below the nonfacilitated level.
source: (There must also be a third state, synaptic depression, in which the strength of the sensorimotor connection is reduced below the nonfacilitated level [Montarolo et al., 1988].)
evidence: This is an inference based on known phenomena in Aplysia, supported by citation.

claim: Several studies have reported stability of some dendritic spines for periods of weeks-to-months after training in mice.
source: Several such studies have reported stability of some dendritic spines for periods of weeks-to-months after training (Xu et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2009; Liston et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about findings from other studies, supported by citations.

claim: Spines in the adult mammalian cortex exhibit little turnover.
source: These results, as well as evidence that spines in the adult mammalian cortex exhibit little turnover (Grutzendler et al., 2002), have led some to argue that stable spines provide a physical basis for the lifelong maintenance of memories (Bhatt et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement about findings from other studies, supported by citations.

claim: Other studies of the mouse brain using very similar in vivo imaging techniques have reported a high degree of spine instability in the adult cerebral cortex.
source: But other studies of the mouse brain using very similar in vivo imaging techniques have reported a high degree of spine instability in the adult cerebral cortex (Trachtenberg et al., 2002; Holtmaat et al., 2005); the contradiction between these two sets of opposed findings remains unresolved.
evidence: This is a statement about findings from other studies, supported by citations.

claim: Even in those studies where spines of adult cortical neurons were reported to be highly stable, there was significant instability of both pre-existing and new spines within the first 2–4 days after a training protocol.
source: Furthermore, even in those studies where spines of adult cortical neurons were reported to be highly stable, there was significant instability of both pre-existing and new spines within the first 2–4 days after a training protocol (Xu et al., 2009; Yang et al., 2009), and we monitored SN varicosities for only 48 hr after training with 5HT.
evidence: This is a statement about findings from other studies, supported by citations.

claim: LTS could be fully reinstated following its disruption by the same antimnemonic treatments previously shown to eliminate LTF.
source: We found that LTS could be fully reinstated following its disruption by the same antimnemonic treatments previously shown to eliminate LTF (Cai et al., 2011, 2012; Lee et al., 2012; Hu and Schacher, 2014) (Figures 7 and 8).
evidence: This is a key finding from the behavioral experiments, shown in Figures 7 and 8.

claim: The LTM for sensitization may be intact in animals following reconsolidation blockade and inhibition of PKM, despite the elimination of both behavioral enhancement and synaptic growth.
source: First, the LTM for sensitization may be intact in animals following reconsolidation blockade and inhibition of PKM, despite the elimination of both behavioral enhancement and synaptic growth.
evidence: This is one possible explanation for the reinstatement findings.

claim: According to one scheme, synapses serve merely to express LTM, they are not sites of LTM storage.
source: According to this scheme, synapses serve merely to express LTM, they are not sites of LTM storage.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: The reinstatement of LTM expression involves restoring the appropriate number of synapses between the SNs and MNs, as determined by an experience-registering homeostatic mechanism.
source: The reinstatement of LTM expression, then, involves restoring the appropriate number of synapses between the SNs and MNs, as determined by an experience-registering homeostatic mechanism.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Reconsolidation blockade and inhibition of PKM can erase the stored sensitization memory through the reversal of pre- and postsynaptic structures induced by the long-term training, but the antimnemonic treatments do not eliminate the primer.
source: The second possible explanation incorporates the notion of an as-yet-unidentified priming mechanism; here, reconsolidation blockade and inhibition of PKM, can erase the stored sensitization memory through the reversal of pre- and postsynaptic structures induced by the long-term training, but the antimnemonic treatments do not eliminate the primer.
evidence: This is an alternative speculative explanation for the findings.

claim: The primer does not constitute LTM, but is required for its reconstitution via new synaptic growth.
source: The primer does not constitute LTM, but is required for its reconstitution via new synaptic growth.
evidence: This is part of the speculative priming explanation.

claim: In a previous study, the authors attempted to reinstate LTS following its disruption by inhibition of PKM Apl III but failed.
source: In a previous study we attempted to reinstate LTS following its disruption by inhibition of PKM Apl III but failed (Cai et al., 2011) (see Figure 3B of the earlier study).
evidence: This is a reference to a previous finding by the authors.

claim: The authors used only a single bout of tail shocks in their previous failed attempt to reinstate LTS.
source: Interestingly, we used only a single bout of tail shocks in that attempt.
evidence: This is a statement about the methods used in a previous study.

claim: One bout of tails shocks is insufficient to fully recruit the signaling pathways that reinstate LTS.
source: In light of the present results (Figures 7 and 8), our previous failure indicates that one bout of tails shocks is insufficient to fully recruit the signaling pathways that reinstate LTS (Abel et al., 1998; Sossin, 2008; Mayford et al., 2012; Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the current and previous results.

claim: The data from behavioral experiments involving the use of an HDAC inhibitor implicate epigenetic modifications in the storage mechanism for LTM in Aplysia.
source: The data from our behavioral experiments involving the use of an HDAC inhibitor (Figure 9) implicate epigenetic modifications (Levenson and Sweatt 2005; Rahn et al., 2013; Graff and Tsai 2013a)—either in the SN or MN or, most likely, both—in the storage mechanism for LTM in Aplysia.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the TSA experiments, shown in Figure 9.

claim: Data from an in vitro study of LTF have also implicated histone acetylation in LTM in Aplysia.
source: Data from an in vitro study of LTF have also implicated histone acetylation in LTM in Aplysia (Guan et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a statement about findings from another study, supported by citation.

claim: TSA, by inhibiting histone deacetylase, activates the transcription of genes that promote LTM; the activation of these genes, in turn, may compensate for a disruptive action of chelerythrine on LTM.
source: Possibly, TSA, by inhibiting histone deacetylase, activates the transcription of genes that promote LTM; the activation of these genes, in turn, may compensate for a disruptive action of chelerythrine on LTM.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for how TSA blocks chelerythrine's effects.

claim: Treatment with an HDAC inhibitor rescues cognitive deficits and learning-related synaptic plasticity in mice that are heterozygous for a mutant form of CREB binding protein (CBP).
source: Thus, treatment with an HDAC inhibitor rescues cognitive deficits and learning-related synaptic plasticity in mice that are heterozygous for a mutant form of CREB binding protein (CBP) (Alarcon et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a statement about findings from another study, supported by citation.

claim: Phosphorylation of CBP by the atypical PKCζ is required for the histone acetylation that promotes the differentiation of developing neural precursors into neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes.
source: In addition, it has been found that phosphorylation of CBP by the atypical PKCζ is required for the histone acetylation that promotes the differentiation of developing neural precursors into neurons, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes; mutant mice haploinsufficient for CBP exhibit abnormal development of the cerebral cortex (Wang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about findings from another study, supported by citation.
